name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Rabb won the Democratic primary in a heavily Democratic seat
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: The D+40 district makes a Democratic hold overwhelming; the only general-election opponent is an independent who has raised about $10,800, while Rabb raised over $1.3 million and drew substantial outside support. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or an unusually strong independent campaign could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
This Philadelphia-based House seat is one of the most Democratic districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+40. Dwight Evans is retiring, and Chris Rabb emerges from the Democratic primary as the heavy favorite to hold the seat. The only general-election opponent is independent Dennis Mahoney, who has raised just over $10,000 and has no outside support.

Rabb raised more than $1.3 million and benefited from about $1.6 million in outside spending, while prediction markets put his chances of winning at roughly 96%. With no expert ratings or general-election polls available, the forecast rests on the district's overwhelming partisan fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
